name: Office of U.S. Senator Angela Alsobrooks
subject: Senator Alsobrooks Newsletter -- Government Shutdown: 24 Days
body:
|

---
Friends and neighbors, It's been 24 days since the Republicans shut down the federal government, inflicting harm on hundreds of thousands of Maryland civil servants and the millions of Americans they serve. The Republicans know what's at stake and are asking Democrats to vote to let them continue what they are doing. That is not an option. This month, countless Americans have begun to receive notice that their health insurance costs are going up. Yesterday, Republicans tried to pass a bill that would allow the President to cherry-pick which federal employees could get paid during this Republican-sponsored government shutdown. Let me make this clear: every single federal worker should be getting paid. It is not their fault that Republicans have chosen to shut down the government. That's why yesterday, [I spoke on the Senate Floor](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fSen_Alsobrooks%2fstatus%2f1981409422586106318&redir_log=874601011961332) advocating for Republicans to pass legislation I introduced alongside Senator Van Hollen called the _True Shutdown Fairness Act_ , which would pay all federal employees - both those excepted and furloughed - as well as service members and federal contractors during the current Republican-led shutdown and would also prevent the Administration's attempts at mass firings (Reductions in Force or RIFs) while the government is shut down. Senator Van Hollen introduced the legislation and I joined him on the floor to ask for its passage, but Republicans blocked it. We must pass legislation that ensures our federal workers receive the paychecks they earned. Around 750,000 federal employees have been furloughed this month - at no fault of their own. The Republican bill would ignore these dedicated workers, leaving them to continue to go without a paycheck while President Trump refuses to get back to the bargaining table. They can't afford to wait for the President to tire of throwing celebratory picnics or tearing down the White House for a gilded ballroom. In case some of my colleagues on the other side of the aisle have forgotten - federal workers don't just serve Democrats. They serve every American citizen who needs their help. Researching cures for cancer isn't just for people who live in blue states. Making sure people get their Social Security checks isn't some left wing conspiracy. I would assume that everyone in this body agrees that Americans should get paid for their labor. Well, if you believe that, you will support our bill. This legislation has been endorsed by the American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE), the National Treasury Employees Union (NTEU), the National Federation of Federal Employees (NFFE), the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees (AFSCME), the International Federation of Professional and Technical Engineers (IFPTE), the Partnership for Public Service, and the American Federation of Labor and Congress of Industrial Organizations (AFL-CIO). I will continue to fight alongside my Democratic colleagues to get our government back open, while ensuring that Marylanders and Americans can continue to have access to affordable health care - something the Republicans have made clear they do not consider a priority. **Continuing to Build the Case Against Secretary Kennedy Despite Shutdown** As you may remember earlier this summer, I, along with Senator Ron Wyden, released a 54-page report chronicling every day of RFK Jr.'s costly, chaotic, and corrupt reign as HHS Secretary. Senator Wyden and I continue to build the case for why RFK Jr. must resign or be fired. Despite the Republican shutdown, RFK Jr. continues to harm the American people. We will continue to release updated actions taken by RFK Jr. and add these acts to our [joint report](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.msnbc.com%2fmorning-joe%2fwatch%2f-dangerous-for-america-senator-says-rfk-jr-has-to-go-246682181595&redir_log=889323476374688). Chaos, Corruption, and Costs Continues: Kennedy's Latest Failings **Below are Kennedy 's latest harmful actions (from October 10-October 23, 2025)**:
1. The Trump health care shutdown drags on as Senate Republicans once again voted down legislation to reopen the federal government, permanently extend middle-class tax credits that make Affordable Care Act (ACA) premiums affordable, repeal Republicans' largest health care cuts in history, and protect against reckless and unlawful funding cancellations. As open enrollment nears and even more Americans learn their families face catastrophic premium spikes next year, Kennedy stands idly by, allowing a health care affordability crisis to unfold nationwide. Republicans refuse to reopen the federal government and avert a health care crisis that will cause health care premiums to [double, on average](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.kff.org%2faffordable-care-act%2faca-marketplace-premium-payments-would-more-than-double-on-average-next-year-if-enhanced-premium-tax-credits-expire%2f&redir_log=982798029351089), and even triple or quadruple for working and middle-class Americans. Kennedy is entirely absent as this crisis unfolds, not unlike House Republicans who refuse to even show up for work.
2. Kennedy's anti-science crusade continues as his hand-picked conspiracy theorists and vaccine skeptics, who now make up the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP), [announced they would form a workgroup](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fthehill.com%2fpolicy%2fhealthcare%2f5548074-cdc-panel-to-review-childhood-vaccine-schedules%2f&redir_log=665678693172646) to revisit the childhood vaccine schedule, threatening access to life-saving vaccines for children.
3. Spurred by the White House and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Director Vought's cruel shutdown agenda, Kennedy continues his campaign to gut HHS by [laying off approximately 1,760 employees](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fthehill.com%2fnewsletters%2f5555910-the-final-tally-on-chaotic-hhs-layoffs%2f&redir_log=938422414604539), including civil servants that worked on Measles response and produce the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report, nearly double the figure projected previously by administration officials. Blaming the initial oversight on "data discrepancies and processing errors," HHS [has rescinded hundreds of erroneous layoffs](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.axios.com%2f2025%2f10%2f15%2ftrump-hhs-laid-off-employees-government-shutdown-cdc&redir_log=206319857422590) at the Centers for Disease Control - the latest example of Kennedy causing chaos at the agency.
4. As a part of the [illegal](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.fox5dc.com%2fnews%2fillegal-capricious-federal-judge-attempting-halt-firings-federal-workers&redir_log=12181155487708) shutdown firings, Kennedy fired staff that operate the Community Services Block Grant, a program that provides funds to states and local nonprofits to reduce poverty and revitalize low-income communities. Kennedy [fired](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fabcnews.go.com%2fPolitics%2fmental-health-substance-abuse-staffers-fired-amid-government%2fstory%3fid%3d126510787&redir_log=568601523993752) more than 100 people from the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration, gutting the agency responsible for addressing our nation's mental health care and substance use crises to half the size it was at the beginning of the year. Kennedy fired employees at the division of Healthy Start at the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), a program which prevents maternal deaths and reduces infant mortality. Kennedy [laid off everyone](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.notus.org%2fhealth-science%2fhhs-office-population-affairs-family-planning&redir_log=032271048373581) that managed the Title X Family Planning Program and the Teen Pregnancy Prevention Program, which together serve low-income and uninsured individuals, offering services like contraception, STI prevention, and family planning. Kennedy fired the HRSA staff tasked with operating the Emergency Medical Services (EMS) for Children program which prevents pediatric deaths.
5. The shutdown has [forced some hospitals](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fsubscriber.politicopro.com%2farticle%2f2025%2f10%2fhospital-at-home-program-collateral-damage-of-the-shutdown-00602997&redir_log=150302157634790) to withdraw from the Acute Hospital Care at Home initiative, which allows hospitals to remotely monitor thousands of seriously-ill but stable patients at home, freeing up hospital beds for other patients. Kennedy has already enabled massive cuts to hospitals through his support of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act - this is the latest way Kennedy's Department is exacerbating a health care crisis across the country.
6. The Food and Drug Administration [published](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.fda.gov%2findustry%2ffda-user-fee-programs%2fcenter-drug-evaluation-and-research-center-biologics-evaluation-and-research-net-hiring-data-fy-2023%3futm_campaign%3ddc_diagnosis%26utm_medium%3demail%26_hsenc%3dp2ANqtz-8Ia4Bx61lRjmVnUfN0q-0a0ziWGXamWdD95UHQnlbE0wKi-6Yng7V4CL2hYfUvowDwOCNrQEAmMDqNewHRMfU0d1I6xXID3Z0TN-ksUHN_6oLZq0o%26_hsmi%3d386042570%26utm_content%3d386042570%26utm_source%3dhs_email&redir_log=540985600032662) its latest personnel numbers, reflecting that in fiscal year 2025, the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research lost 1,093 people and the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research lost 224. [Reporting](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.statnews.com%2fpharmalot%2f2025%2f10%2f20%2ffda-drug-approvals-slowing-rejections-rising%2f%3futm_campaign%3ddc_diagnosis%26utm_medium%3demail%26_hsenc%3dp2ANqtz-_YRVLK101KL-Yu_5oasTLr5BbibO7sspfK1ZU_isfDZfPYFZ-ZzaBHaTm8Mpm0efinnGZqaEeArhT9RMAbn31Z5zgZ9osbsBLle5zXy_an_CoqgV0%26_hsmi%3d386042570%26utm_content%3d386042570%26utm_source%3dhs_email&redir_log=383900179882281) found that these widespread staffing cuts and losses due to Kennedy's actions have led to a slowdown of the FDA's review of drugs and delayed review of applications. These cuts are taking a toll on health care jobs nationwide. **FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS**
_This information will continue to be updated._

WILL FEDERAL WORKERS AND CONTRACTORS BE PAID DURING THE SHUTDOWN?
* Federal employees will not receive paychecks during a government shutdown. However, because of legislation my predecessor Senator Ben Cardin and Maryland's Senior Senator Chris Van Hollen shepherded into law after the 2019 Trump shutdown, federal workers are guaranteed to automatically receive back pay when the government reopens. Unfortunately, this backpay is not guaranteed for federal contract workers. I have worked alongside Senators Van Hollen and Blumenthal to right this wrong and ensure federal contract workers are paid.

WHAT IS A GOVERNMENT SHUTDOWN?
* According to the [Congressional Research Service](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.congress.gov%2fcrs-product%2fR41759&redir_log=004355365006287), when federal government agencies and programs lack budget authority after the expiration of either full-year or interim appropriations, they experience a "funding gap."
* Under the Antideficiency Act (31 U.S.C. §§1341 et seq.), they must cease operations, except in certain circumstances when continued activities are authorized by law. When there is a funding gap that affects many federal entities, the situation is often referred to as a government shutdown.
* Due to the lapse in funding, many Federal agencies may have to furlough workers and would have limited capacity to work on cases.
* However, my office remains open and ready to assist you.
* Due to the shutdown, depending on decisions from the Trump Administration, some Federal agencies may not begin working on your case immediately, but our office will do our best to get you the assistance you need in a timely manner.

WILL I STILL RECEIVE MY SOCIAL SECURITY BENEFITS?
* Yes, according to the Social Security Administration, recipients will continue to receive Social Security benefits and SSI checks.

WILL I STILL RECEIVE MY MEDICARE AND/OR MEDICAID BENEFITS?
* Yes, Medicare and Medicaid recipients will still receive benefits.
However, you will not be able to get a new or replacement Medicare card, and benefit verifications will stop.

WILL THE CHILDREN'S HEALTH INSURANCE PROGRAM (CHIP) BE AFFECTED?
* No. According to CMS's FY26 contingency plan, CMS will maintain the staff necessary to make payments for the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP).

WILL I STILL RECEIVE MY VETERANS' BENEFITS?
* Per VA guidance, the following will not be impacted by the shutdown:
VA Medical Centers, Outpatient Clinics, and Vet Centers will be open as usual and providing all services.
* VA benefits will continue to be processed and delivered, including compensation, pension, education, and housing benefits.
* Burials will continue at VA national cemeteries. Applications for headstones, markers, and burial benefits processing will continue.
* The Board of Veterans' Appeals will continue decisions on Veterans' cases.
* Call Centers: The VA's primary call center (1-800-MyVA411) and the Veterans Crisis Line (Dial 988, Press 1) are open 24/7.

_Per VA guidance, the following services will be impacted:_
* VA will not provide Veteran career counseling or transition assistance program activities.
* Call Centers: The GI Bill Hotline (1-888-GIBILL-1) will be closed and National Cemetery Applicant Assistance (1-800-697-6947) hotline will be closed.
* VA benefits regional offices will be closed.
* VA will cease public affairs and outreach to Veterans, including social media, VetResources emails, and responses to press inquiries.
* VA will not permanently place headstones or maintain the grounds at VA national cemeteries.
* VA will not process applications for pre-need burials at VA cemeteries.
* VA will not print new presidential memorial certificates.
* VA will cease outreach to state, county, tribal, municipal, faith-based, and community-based partners by the VA Central Office.

For more information, please [visit the VA's website here](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fdepartment.va.gov%2fcontingency-planning%2f&redir_log=258908356363333).

WILL ACTIVE-DUTY SERVICEMEMBERS BE PAID?
* According to Department of Defense guidance, active duty servicemembers do not receive their paychecks during a shutdown but will continue working as they are deemed "essential."
* Servicemembers will receive back pay, but paycheck deposits will be delayed.
* If you live in base housing, your services will remain intact.
* Schools operated by the Department of Defense Education Activity (DoDEA) will remain open.
* On-base Child Development Centers will close on a case-by-case basis. Please check locally for closures.
* Civilian personnel who are necessary to carry out expected activities will continue to work, but also will not be paid, and some civilian personnel will be furloughed without pay.
* USAA offers [interest-free loans](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.usaa.com%2finet%2fwc%2fent-gov-shutdown-assistance-landing-mkt&redir_log=75513517742480) and Navy Federal Credit Union offers [paycheck assistance](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.navyfederal.org%2fabout%2fpress-releases%2f2024%2fnavy-federal-offers-paycheck-relief-to-members-impacted-by-government-shutdown.html&redir_log=397786780427962) to servicemembers and DoD civilians during a shutdown.

WHAT HAPPENS TO SNAP/WIC BENEFITS?
* SNAP benefits may be delayed as of November 1 if the Republican shutdown continues.
* WIC operations are not impacted at this time.

WILL HEAD START PROGRAMS CLOSE?
* Most Head Start programs are not expected to be impacted by the Federal shutdown.

WHAT HAPPENS TO FEDERAL LOANS DURING A SHUTDOWN?
* The Pell Grant and Federal Direct Student Loan programs are considered mandatory, meaning the programs can still make payments during a shutdown.
* However, staff may be furloughed, so assistance may be delayed.

WHAT HAPPENS TO PROGRAMS WITHIN THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE?
* According to USDA, the Department will continue operations related to: certain farm loan processing items, certain natural resource and conservation programs, core nutrition safety net programs, essential food safety operations (inspections and laboratory work) to protect public health, responding to and preparing for wildland fires, activities supported by user fees (including grading, assessment, inspection, import and export), animal and plant health emergency programs (including new world screwworm, highly pathogenic avian influenza, exotic fruit flies, African swine fever, and rabies), Section 521 Rental Assistance Program outlays of prior obligations, human resource policies and systems, critical IT infrastructure and cybersecurity, emergency operations, and national defense and homeland security readiness.
* According to USDA, the Department will cease operations related to: payment processing, disaster assistance processing, technical assistance, contracts and agreements not related to exempted programs, financial management beyond funds management, regulatory work, travel, trainings, trade negotiations, timber sales, hazardous fuels treatments, special use permits, surveys for high-risk plant pests and diseases for certain swine, cattle, and aquatic animal diseases, long-term studies and research on animal diseases, research and report publications, website updates, data products, and the majority of Risk Management Agency, Natural Resources Conservation Service, Foreign Agricultural Service, Food and Nutrition Service, National Institute of Food and Agriculture, Economic Research Service, National Agricultural Statistical Service, Rural Development, and Staff Office activities.

HOW IS THE SMALL BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION (SBA) IMPACTED?
* The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) will pause most new business loan approvals and program support during a government shutdown -- including 7(a) and 504 loans.
* However, SBA's disaster loan processing is expected to continue.
* The SBA has published its "Plan for Operating in the Event of a Lapse in Appropriations - September 2025." For more information, please [visit the SBA's website here](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.sba.gov%2fsba-employee-information-shutdown-furlough&redir_log=244887925198446).

WILL TSA SECURITY LINES BE LONGER AT THE AIRPORT?
* Most TSA airport personnel and FAA air traffic controllers would be required to continue working, without pay, during a shutdown.
* However, airports may experience longer-than-usual security lines, so please plan to arrive early for any travel.

CAN I STILL GET A NEW PASSPORT DURING A SHUTDOWN?
* Yes, passport applications will continue to be processed, but please note, response times may be longer than usual.

**Unemployment: **
Federal employees and contractors that have been furloughed because of the federal shutdown may file an unemployment claim. Your claim must be filed in the jurisdiction of your duty station. (Please note: If you receive retroactive pay, you will be required to repay all unemployment benefits. Eligibility determinations are made by each unemployment insurance agency.)

Workers with a duty station in Maryland should contact the Maryland Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation at (410) 853-1700 or click [here](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2flabor.maryland.gov%2funemployment-insurance%2f&redir_log=37025617561357). You may find this list of [Frequently Asked Questions](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2flabor.maryland.gov%2funemployment-insurance%2fclaimants%2ffederal-employees%2ffrequently-asked-questions.shtml&redir_log=887999654645787) for federal employees on the Department's website helpful. Federal employees who are excepted and continue to work are not eligible for unemployment. I, along with Senator Van Hollen and Congresswoman Elfreth have introduced legislation to expand eligibility to every federal employee.

[United Way's 211.org](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.211.org%2f&redir_log=551546052297128) can direct you to local resources for assistance with housing and utility expenses, food, healthcare, and other emergency situations.

The Maryland Department of Labor also offers a Federal Worker Emergency Loan Program for federal employees recently terminated from their position. More information can be found [here](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2flabor.maryland.gov%2ffederalworkers%2fFWEloan%2f&redir_log=68485812082349). The Federal Employee Education and Assistance Fund offers [Shutdown Grants](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2ffeea.org%2fshutdown%2f%23toggle-id-2&redir_log=933130865581257) for qualifying full-time federal civilian employees. The application will only become available should a shutdown persist beyond the point that federal employees miss all or part of a paycheck.

**Utility Assistance: **
* BGE [Assistance Resource Finder](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.bge.com%2fmy-account%2fcustomer-support%2fbill-help&redir_log=846267117825404)
* Pepco: [Assistance Programs (Maryland)](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fthesource.pepcoholdings.com%2fexpanded-support-available-during-federal-government-shutdown-3%2f&redir_log=859716136495703)
* WSSC: [Financial Assistance Programs](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.wsscwater.com%2fassistance&redir_log=380993903065259)
* Washington Gas: [Energy Assistance Programs](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.washingtongas.com%2fget-assistance%2fenergy-assistance&redir_log=355951803248443)
* Potomac Edison: [Energy Assistance Programs](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.firstenergycorp.com%2fcontent%2fdam%2fcustomer%2fbillinserts%2f2023-05%2520MD%2520Energy%2520Assistance%25200523.pdf&redir_log=782621310575711)

**Financial Institution Guidance: ** The Federal Housing Administration has called on lenders to be sensitive to the financial hardships experienced by borrowers because of the shutdown. This includes offering forbearance agreements (agreeing to delay foreclosure), waiving late fees, and other options. Please contact your financial institution for specifics. Many banks, credit unions and mortgage companies are offering services to federal workers that are customers and members facing financial difficulty due to the shutdown. These services can include reversing fees, offering low-interest loans and due date extensions.

* The [Navy Federal Credit Union ](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.navyfederal.org%2fabout%2fgovernment-shutdown.php%3fintcmp%3dhp%257Ccont%257C4%257Cclns%257Cshutdown%257Cgovshutdown%257C12%2f22%2f2018%257C%257C%257C&redir_log=815287163708845)is offering interest-free shutdown loan assistance to members and other federal government employees.
* The [Congressional Federal Credit Union](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.congressionalfcu.org%2floans%2fpersonal-loans%2ffurlough-solutions&redir_log=707528381395518) is offering interest-free Furlough Relief loans for eligible members during the shutdown.
* The [U.S. Employees Credit Union](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.myusecu.org%2fhome&redir_log=558262161358199) is offering interest-free shutdown loans to eligible members.

Some local credit unions are offering assistance during the shutdown. If you belong to a credit union, please contact them to find out if they are offering any assistance.

Federal Student Aid:
* The Federal Employee Education and Assistance Fund offers emergency loans to federal employees. More [here](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2ffeea.org%2four-programs%2femergency-loans%2f%23hardships&redir_log=526796067056396).

**Nutrition Assistance** For a comprehensive list of food banks across Maryland, click [here](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15529.13200679.5715581.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fdhs.maryland.gov%2fcommunity-resources-page%2ffood-bank%2f&redir_log=332606395569420). **You may need to show a government work ID for some locations**. **Stay in the Fight ** We will not give up. I ask that you continue to fight alongside us. Please continue to reach out to us. You can call the office, connect with us, or follow us on Bluesky, Instagram, Facebook, Threads, YouTube, and X. We are in this TOGETHER.

Sincerely,

Angela D. Alsobrooks
United States Senator

According to the , when federal government agencies and programs lack budget authority after the expiration of either full-year or interim appropriations, they experience a "funding gap." Under the Antideficiency Act (31 U.S.C. §§1341 et seq.), they must cease operations, except in certain circumstances when continued activities are authorized by law. When there is a funding gap that affects many federal entities, the situation is often referred to as a government shutdown. Call Centers: The VA's primary call center (1-800-MyVA411) and the Veterans Crisis Line (Dial 988, Press 1) are open 24/7. Per VA guidance, the following services will be impacted: VA will not provide Veteran career counseling or transition assistance program activities. Call Centers: The GI Bill Hotline (1-888-GIBILL-1) will be closed and National Cemetery Applicant Assistance (1-800-697-6947) hotline will be closed. VA benefits regional offices will be closed. VA will cease public affairs and outreach to Veterans, including social media, VetResources emails, and responses to press inquiries. VA will not permanently place headstones or maintain the grounds at VA national cemeteries. VA will not process applications for pre-need burials at VA cemeteries. VA will not print new presidential memorial certificates. VA will cease outreach to state, county, tribal, municipal, faith-based, and community-based partners by the VA Central Office. For more information, please . WILL ACTIVE-DUTY SERVICEMEMBERS BE PAID? According to Department of Defense guidance, active duty servicemembers do not receive their paychecks during a shutdown but will continue working as they are deemed "essential." Servicemembers will receive back pay, but paycheck deposits will be delayed. If you live in base housing, your services will remain intact. Schools operated by the Department of Defense Education Activity (DoDEA) will remain open. On-base Child Development Centers will close on a case-by-case basis. Please check locally for closures. Civilian personnel who are necessary to carry out expected activities will continue to work, but also will not be paid, and some civilian personnel will be furloughed without pay. SNAP benefits may be delayed as of November 1 if the Republican shutdown continues. WIC operations are not impacted at this time. WILL HEAD START PROGRAMS CLOSE? Most Head Start programs are not expected to be impacted by the Federal shutdown. WHAT HAPPENS TO FEDERAL LOANS DURING A SHUTDOWN? The Pell Grant and Federal Direct Student Loan programs are considered mandatory, meaning the programs can still make payments during a shutdown. However, staff may be furloughed, so assistance may be delayed. WHAT HAPPENS TO PROGRAMS WITHIN THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE? According to USDA, the Department will continue operations related to: certain farm loan processing items, certain natural resource and conservation programs, core nutrition safety net programs, essential food safety operations (inspections and laboratory work) to protect public health, responding to and preparing for wildland fires, activities supported by user fees (including grading, assessment, inspection, import and export), animal and plant health emergency programs (including new world screwworm, highly pathogenic avian influenza, exotic fruit flies, African swine fever, and rabies), Section 521 Rental Assistance Program outlays of prior obligations, human resource policies and systems, critical IT infrastructure and cybersecurity, emergency operations, and national defense and homeland security readiness. HOW IS THE SMALL BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION (SBA) IMPACTED? The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) will pause most new business loan approvals and program support during a government shutdown -- including 7(a) and 504 loans. However, SBA's disaster loan processing is expected to continue. The SBA has published its "Plan for Operating in the Event of a Lapse in Appropriations - September 2025." For more information, please . WILL TSA SECURITY LINES BE LONGER AT THE AIRPORT? Most TSA airport personnel and FAA air traffic controllers would be required to continue working, without pay, during a shutdown. However, airports may experience longer-than-usual security lines, so please plan to arrive early for any travel. CAN I STILL GET A NEW PASSPORT DURING A SHUTDOWN? Yes, passport applications will continue to be processed, but please note, response times may be longer than usual. CAN I STILL GET A GUIDED TOUR OF THE U.S. CAPITOL OR WHITE HOUSE? Unfortunately, due to the federal shutdown, all federal buildings will be closed for the duration of the shutdown. This week, North Carolina's legislature passed a new congressional map. Because our governor isn't allowed to veto redistricting bills (a quirk of NC law), that map is now in effect.
There will be many legal challenges to this map. More broadly, this is a truly unfortunate trend in American politics. The particular target of this effort was Rep. Don Davis - a friend of mine and genuinely good guy. We served in Congress together. He constantly looks for ways to reach across the aisle and is _incentivized to do so_ because his district is competitive. They're trying to replace him with someone who won't need to listen to the other side. If you scale that up across all of Congress, you see why things have gotten so extreme.
That's why the _first bill_ I ever filed in the state legislature was to end gerrymandering. This practice belongs in the dustbin of history - the sooner, the better.
### **Our new EPA lawsuit**
We just filed a lawsuit against the EPA.
Why?
Because they owe North Carolina $150 million.
Here's the situation:
A few years ago, Congress gave the EPA some money and basically told them, "We want you to use this to help low income families pay for solar panels, if they want them. If they don't want them, that's fine, but we think this will bring down their energy bill by several hundred dollars a year, so we want to give them the option."
Those funds were set to go to about 12,000 families in our state, mainly in low-income and rural communities.
Then Congress passed the Big Beautiful Bill, which made a lot of cuts, but - and this part is crucial - also said that the EPA could not cut any money that _had already been awarded to a state._
And this payment of $150m _had already been awarded_ to our state. It was literally in an account with our state's name on it.
The EPA will say that because the money hasn't been spent yet, they're allowed to cancel it.
But that's wrong. Congress has the power to cancel it, but the EPA doesn't. Congress was explicit about that.
Which means this case isn't really about solar panels - it's about whether a federal agency can ignore the law.
That's why, on behalf of the state of North Carolina, I'm asking the court to order the EPA to release the $150 million it owes us. I'll let you know how it goes.
### **The Kars-R-Us Scam**
It's breast cancer awareness month, so it's a perfect time to tell you about a scam charity operation we just shut down.
It was called Kars-R-Us. Their pitch was if you donated your car, they'd sell it and use the proceeds to help women get breast cancer screenings.
Remarkably, over 80,000 people donated their cars. That generated over $45 million in revenue.
And how much went to breast cancer screenings?
Only $126,000.

_Less than 1%._
So we teamed up with Secretary of State Elaine Marshall, took them to court, won a major settlement and blocked them from ever being able to do that again.
### **Our Lighthouse Fund**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/be5747e5-99ac-416a-997e-c8cd20f6753b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Because I can 't shake hands with everyone, I need your help._
It's been a few months since I mentioned this, so a quick reminder:
We're thinking ahead. A small investment now could be very helpful later.
Our Lighthouse Fund lets us digitally advertise one video message per month to a big chunk of independent voters in NC. (Here's an [example](https://substack.com/redirect/f5b9f4f7-38fe-44ec-829b-852e4eabeec3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).)
These are the voters who will decide our next election, and staying in front of them - at a low but consistent level, like a lighthouse shining its beacon in the dark - is one of the smartest investments we can make. We can't afford to slip from their radar for the next few years.
More than **2,000** of you are already supporting this effort. If you'd like to learn more - or continue to support us - you can do so **[here](https://substack.com/redirect/0dcd2b9d-4a98-4726-94bf-7ca572d82b91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** (ActBlue) or **[here](https://substack.com/redirect/00e8b04a-2cc0-4b5e-b095-f14abb82ac0b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** (non-ActBlue).
Best,
Jeff

The Guardian: Trump’s justice department appointees remove leadership of voting unit [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=102425_2&amount=25]
This speaks for itself, folks. Straight from The Guardian :
" Donald Trump’s appointees at the Department of Justice have removed all of the senior civil servants working as managers in the department’s voting section and directed attorneys to dismiss all active cases, according to people familiar with the matter, part of a broader attack on the department’s civil rights division. "
This action represents a dramatic escalation in Trump's war on voting , coming after he ordered a permanent litigation freeze on voting cases back in January and then issued his suppressive, anti-voting executive order last month.
It's worth noting that the staff removed are nonpartisan civil servants -- lawyers who are career DOJ employees and serve regardless of who is president. Any partisan presidential appointees from the Biden administration ended their jobs when Trump was inaugurated and have been gone for months.
Are we surprised? No. But this action -- though expected, based on how this division was sidelined in Trump's first four years -- highlights how badly we need to fight for our fundamental rights as citizens , from the outside of government.

The civil rights division, which was created in 1957 and is often referred to as the “crown jewel” of the justice department, has always been a cornerstone in the fight to protect our right to vote.
But when Trump campaign lawyer and election denier Harmeet Dhillon -- who has argued in court in favor of voter suppression laws -- was confirmed to lead the department last month, she sent out new “mission statements” that made it clear the civil rights division was shifting its focus from protecting the civil rights of marginalized people to supporting Trump’s priorities.
You don't have to read into that to get the message: Our fundamental rights, including voting and so much more, aren't going to be protected by this administration. In fact, they're going to be repeatedly attacked from within our government until they ensconce their control forever.

body:
We say HELL NO!

| | | | |
---
| | Derek,

It’s official — leading New Hampshire Democrats are now openly calling for an **income tax on every working Granite Stater.**
---
[](https://5wbjs096.r.us-east-1.awstrack.me/L0/https:%2F%2Fsecure.winred.com%2Fgranitesolutions%2Fdonate/1/0100019a16c551ba-5db7bd94-b7bb-4218-9e61-c45ead465280-000000/bKmprcOqGtH55SQa6akmxBDIYWA=449)
---
| Former Executive Councilor **Andru Volinsky** just published an op-ed arguing that it’s time for New Hampshire to adopt a _3% income tax_ to fund their runaway spending.
For generations, we’ve said that would never happen here.

Now, they’re saying the unthinkable is _“thinkable.”_ Let me be clear:
👉 **There will be no income tax in New Hampshire — not on my watch.** New Hampshire’s success comes from doing things differently. We balance our budgets, keep government small, and let people keep what they earn. That’s why families and small businesses choose to live here — because we’re the _Live Free or Die_ state, not the _Tax and Spend_ state. But make no mistake — if we don’t fight back right now, the Left will keep pushing until they get what they want: higher taxes, bigger government, and less freedom for you. [That’s why I’m asking you to **stand with me and Granite Solutions** in this fight.

The Attorney General is the only person in our state who can go to court to correct the Governor or the Legislature when they violate the Constitution | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/jaworskifortexas.com/fed-up-14190082?e=5d8d80652b)

| | , The Texas Attorney General is the only person in our state who can go to court to correct the Governor or the Legislature when they violate the Texas or United States Constitution. **That power belongs not to politicians, but to the people.** The AG’s duty is to defend the law only when it is constitutional and just. When it isn’t, the AG has both the right and the responsibility to act. That means if the Governor acts unlawfully, the AG can take him to court. If the Legislature passes an unconstitutional law, the AG can move to overturn it. **It is an enormous power that can do great good—or terrible harm.** We’ve seen what happens when that power is abused. Ken Paxton has used the office for political stunts and personal ambition, from trying to overturn the 2020 election to undermining the Texas Dream Act and hurting thousands of students. **As your next Attorney General, I will use this office for what it was meant to be: an independent voice for the people of Texas. I will defend our constitutions, our freedoms, and our democracy itself.** This office can be the safeguard of our constitutional order, but only if we take it back from those who have corrupted it. [**Chip in today to help us restore integrity to the Texas Attorney General’s office.**](https://jaworskifortexas.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=2e1f50319ad85f5f9e5c11ac9&id=e42393f76f&e=5d8d80652b) Together, we can win. Onward!

**

| Peter,
Since Congress shut down on September 30, federal workers have either been off the job or working without pay. Today, they just missed their second paycheck.
Instead of negotiating an end to the shutdown, Donald Trump and his administration have threatened mass firings, even pledging to renege on a law he signed to guarantee backpay to workers after a shutdown. Trump sees a path to political victory through punishing the workers who keep Social Security working, who make sure our water is safe to drink, and who take care of our veterans.
The people who are working at Social Security offices, still making sure seniors' checks go out on time, won't get their own check this week. Their bills didn't stop. The rent is still due, and they still have families who need to eat. We need solidarity, not charity.
[Our friends at The Labor Force are distributing grocery cards to federal workers during this shutdown. White House Press Secretary **[Karoline Leavitt clashed with CBS reporter Weijia Jiang](https://substack.com/redirect/e1fb4e8b-e0ca-4397-ac39-34fc8371e8f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for falsely saying President Trump is just "tearing down whatever he wants" amid his construction of his new ballroom project.
Leavitt pointed out that many other presidents have undertaken construction and renovation projects at the White House, pulling out photos of past construction. "What do you think that rubble is? How did that rubble get there?" Leavitt quipped back, pointing at an image of a project from the 1950s.

Instead of questioning **[THIS.](https://substack.com/redirect/1552c425-6bdb-4c04-baf5-902ef7284cea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Because it's not whether they did it or not...it's WHAT THEY FOUND once they got there.
**[This presentation](https://substack.com/redirect/1552c425-6bdb-4c04-baf5-902ef7284cea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** reveals a controversial confirmation that...

[Learn More](https://substack.com/redirect/1552c425-6bdb-4c04-baf5-902ef7284cea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
# **Coast Guard opens fire on U-Haul at California base after immigration protest**
U.S. Coast Guard security personnel **[opened fire Thursday night on a U-Haul truck](https://substack.com/redirect/df20595e-2538-4140-9c74-c4771fafc12f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after its driver ignored multiple verbal commands to stop and attempted to back into Coast Guard Base Alameda around 10 p.m., with dramatic video showing flashes of gunfire as the driver then accelerated forward and fled the scene.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/221b3dbb-2a78-4b47-8394-a7e614f3992f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Two hospitalized with gunshot wounds:** The U-Haul had been parked outside the base for most of the day before the incident, and two men arrived at local hospitals with gunshot wounds after the shooting, with one believed to be the driver, according to reports citing sources, though no Coast Guard personnel were injured.
* **Incident follows immigration protests:** The shooting occurred after protests outside the base entrance Thursday where demonstrators attempted to block U.S. Customs and Border Protection agents from entering, with dozens of California Highway Patrol officers in riot gear dispersing the crowd and detaining two people, as the base was meant to serve as a staging area for federal troops before President Trump postponed his planned "surge" to San Francisco.

* * *
# **Kash Patel SLAMS ESPN host** Stephen A. Smith**' s Trump/basketball gambling conspiracy claim**
FBI Director Kash Patel slammed ESPN's Stephen A. Smith on "The Ingraham Angle" for **[suggesting President Trump was behind the arrests of NBA stars and coaches in an illegal gambling scheme,](https://substack.com/redirect/938045d3-aa3e-46a9-84c0-5628c6895ef5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** declaring "I'm the FBI director. I decide which arrest to conduct" and calling Smith's suggestion "the single dumbest thing I've ever heard out of anyone in modern history."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/77650f6f-e276-49a5-aa74-9a27ae9092b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Smith warns of Trump-driven crackdown without evidence:** On ESPN's "First Take," Smith told viewers the arrests were "not coincidental" and warned "more is coming," saying "This is just the tip of the iceberg" and urging "everybody better brace themselves, because he's coming," while referencing possible ICE operations at Bad Bunny's Super Bowl halftime show and listing the WNBA as a potential next target.
* **Historic bust involves 31 arrested in $7 million scheme:** The FBI arrested 31 people including Portland Trail Blazers coach Chauncey Billups, Miami Heat guard Terry Rozier, former NBA player Damon Jones, and members of the Bonanno, Gambino, Genovese, and Lucchese mob families in connection with an illegal gambling operation that netted upward of $7 million over two years.

* * *
# Cheryl Hines Slams Olivia Nuzzi Over RFK Jr. Sexting Scandal: 'Consider the Source'
Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s wife, actress Cheryl Hines, **[explained on"The Katie Miller Podcast"](https://substack.com/redirect/f5f3a0ec-a57a-44a6-80dc-60352b96a9f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that she handled the sexting scandal with former New York Magazine writer Olivia Nuzzi by considering "the source" first, in a cutting putdown of Nuzzi, who lost her job and fiance over the scandal.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/f5f3a0ec-a57a-44a6-80dc-60352b96a9f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Scandal viewed as part of campaign chaos:** Hines characterized last year's digital affair scandal--which Nuzzi admitted was never physical--as part of the noise during Kennedy's presidential campaign, recalling "an exhausting year-and-a-half of headlines and rumors and articles and chaos" and thinking "this is more chaos and more rumors."
* **Questions Nuzzi 's motives for upcoming memoir:** The "Curb Your Enthusiasm" actress questioned Nuzzi's intentions in addressing the scandal again for a memoir expected by year's end, saying "I don't know this person. Don't know their intentions. I could guess, but I won't," while noting that Nuzzi is now at Vanity Fair.
* **Eventually believed Kennedy 's denial:** An insider **[told The NY Post](https://substack.com/redirect/0f5491f0-f365-4363-a674-5aa9146f0feb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that the rumored affair left Hines in "a state of shock and distress" but that she "eventually and emphatically believed, without reservation, Bobby's denial," while Kennedy maintains through his spokesperson that he only met Nuzzi once for an interview that resulted in a "hit piece."

Since Congress shut down on September 30, federal workers have either been off the job or working without pay. Today, they just missed their second paycheck.
| | | | | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001wjMkrhAo09NAqMaLIhLrU18t12CRP0M0t9hZsJ9Zd0WkPz_5brpaRvUZ1r9rGUhB2-mSe86h6dnNbhLhfJfs-lduFd76bgAKmwZr0uqXq23CDCsjYIj71QBar5UN1Qn1l-xDZJjmGEn9Ebv5UpWZWNIg0AhOe1-aOrk1zwrlBxI35VtGFZRjHMcrhQzKiOno3OdicvQvxfgNfXRo8gof9FTdXFPIEkhRd66z6ldbpjbIgXetN6EEXQ==&c=7mRI4Cv0ba87NiQqr-4mmqI9qVY5mGLDh0F2jwKcbhMUS-o9MWn43A==&ch=m2W7LjspPiE3J5pm0vgrZA3Ny1igIQv6_TuZlVG9wWyLprNMlf6Huw==)
---
| Peter,
Since Congress shut down on September 30, federal workers have either been off the job or working without pay. Today, they just missed their second paycheck.
Instead of negotiating an end to the shutdown, Donald Trump and his administration have threatened mass firings, even pledging to renege on a law he signed to guarantee backpay to workers after a shutdown. Trump sees a path to political victory through punishing the workers who keep Social Security working, who make sure our water is safe to drink, and who take care of our veterans.
The people who are working at Social Security offices, still making sure seniors' checks go out on time, won't get their own check this week. Their bills didn't stop. The rent is still due, and they still have families who need to eat. We need solidarity, not charity.
[Our friends at The Labor Force are distributing grocery cards to federal workers during this shutdown. Can you split a donation between Defend Our Courts and Labor Force to buy a load of groceries this week?](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001wjMkrhAo09NAqMaLIhLrU18t12CRP0M0t9hZsJ9Zd0WkPz_5brpaRvUZ1r9rGUhB2-mSe86h6dnNbhLhfJfs-lduFd76bgAKmwZr0uqXq23CDCsjYIj71QBar5UN1Qn1l-xDZJjmGEn9Ebv5UpWZWNIg0AhOe1-aOrk1zwrlBxI35VtGFZRjHMcrhQzKiOno3OdicvQvxfgNfXRo8gof9FTdXFPIEkhRnIUlb7hPOIXHlmlxUux3mQ==&c=7mRI4Cv0ba87NiQqr-4mmqI9qVY5mGLDh0F2jwKcbhMUS-o9MWn43A==&ch=m2W7LjspPiE3J5pm0vgrZA3Ny1igIQv6_TuZlVG9wWyLprNMlf6Huw==)

name: Mikie Sherrill HQ
subject: We made a tough decision
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Andy Kim for New Jersey
body:
Those polls showing a close race are real, and we’re responding.
|
---
| | We'll get right to the point. A recent Emerson poll found this race tied — with tons of undecided voters. It's not an outlier. name: Marie Gluesenkamp Perez
subject: Countless lives saved – including mine
body:
| | Peter,

As it is for so many women, the fight to protect reproductive care is personal for me.

Just a few years ago, I suffered a miscarriage. Planned Parenthood was one of the only places I could turn to get the care I needed, which in this case was an assisted abortion.

Walking through the screaming protesters outside the building made the emotional pain of my loss hurt even more. It was a devastating moment in my life – and an experience I will never forget.

Without access to safe reproductive care, I could have died or suffered complications that could have prevented me from ever going on to have a successful pregnancy.

Ultra-conservative courts and politicians across the country are still hell-bent on dismantling reproductive freedom, with no regard for the countless women who have already suffered as a result.

[A pro-choice Congress is the only answer to this problem – and we can’t make that happen without defending WA-03. Planned Parenthood was one of the only places I could turn to get the care I needed, which in this case was an assisted abortion. Walking through the screaming protesters outside the building made the emotional pain of my loss hurt even more. It was a devastating moment in my life – and an experience I will never forget. Without access to safe reproductive care, I could have died or suffered complications that could have prevented me from ever going on to have a successful pregnancy. subject: Republicans are blocking health care — Medicare for All is the solution.

body:
This shutdown and health care crisis are exactly why we need Medicare for All.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20251024-5554-footer&t=1&akid=5554%2E420207%2EiqZu3J)
Peter,
Working people shouldn’t have to fight for the care they need to survive while insurers profit and politicians play games — yet that’s exactly what’s happening right now.
With Republicans holding the government hostage, health care costs set to skyrocket for millions, and corporations making record profits off our suffering, **the case for Medicare for All has never been stronger.**
[**If you believe health care should be a human right, not a privilege, will you chip in $3 to Pramila’s campaign and help fuel the fight for Medicare for All?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-email-20251024-1.lpU5B8&refcode=em20251024-5554&amount=3&t=2&akid=5554%2E420207%2EiqZu3J)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-email-20251024-1.lpU5B8&amount=3&refcode=em20251024-5554&t=3&akid=5554%2E420207%2EiqZu3J)**
If Republicans refuse to extend critical health care subsidies, premium costs will skyrocket in a few months. **A 50 year old couple making $95,000 a year could see their premiums increase by $17,000 just to keep their current plan.** Millions are already receiving notices that their premiums are set to _double._
Peter, we all know this story too well. The U.S. has some of the worst health outcomes of any advanced economy — millions are uninsured, drowning in medical debt, rationing prescriptions, and living in fear of going bankrupt for getting the care they need.
Meanwhile, insurance companies are making record profits under President Trump, while patients pay more and are denied care more often.
Extending ACA subsidies immediately is urgent and necessary, but it won’t fix a broken system. What we really need is a total reset — a 21st-century health care system that puts people over profits.
**That’s why Pramila is leading the fight for Medicare for All** — to expand and improve Medicare to cover every single person in America with comprehensive care.
By passing the Medicare For All Act, we will ensure that:
* _Everyone_ is able to go to the doctor when they’re sick
* _Everyone_ is able go to the hospital without fear of bankruptcy
* Expensive premiums, deductibles, co-pays, and other out-of-pocket costs are _eliminated completely._
* The U.S. saves _hundreds of billions_ on health expenses annually

From day one, Pramila has fought for Medicare for All and never taken a _dime_ from corporate PACs. That’s why we need your support to take on powerful special interests and build a health care system that works for everyone, we need a strong grassroots movement powering the fight.
**[Please chip in $3 or whatever you can to help fuel this movement and Pramila’s work for Medicare for All.](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-email-20251024-1.lpU5B8&refcode=em20251024-5554&amount=3&t=4&akid=5554%2E420207%2EiqZu3J)**

In solidarity,
Team Pramila

Trump's funding it privately; it's not costing the taxpayer a dime.

They've been up in arms this week, "outraged" that Trump would dare renovate.

My plan to help Coloradans harmed by this crisis.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/117918367/578067689/1239926708?refcode=em_WEI_FR_OpioidCrisis_102425&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjYjFiZmM4Ni1mMmIwLWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=XVfWXVEesWs31sLa_new8m093cuBsjuttEI2i1Qz0Oo=&emci=4523eb90-52b0-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&emdi=cb1bfc86-f2b0-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&ceid=51844520) Back when I first ran to be your Attorney General, I learned something shocking on a visit to Alamosa County, Friend. Over a pancake breakfast at the Campus Café, between bites of a (truly amazing) cinnamon roll, Sheriff Robert Jackson shared with me a stunning fact — that 90% of all inmates in the Alamosa County jail were struggling with opioid use disorder. _And there were no treatment options in the whole San Luis Valley or anywhere nearby._ When I retold what I had learned, it sounded unbelievable to many people. But then, this issue got the attention it deserved, and Colorado journalists began reporting about it. For me, doing nothing was not an option. With the San Luis Valley in mind, my office got to work. So far, we’ve recovered almost **$900 million in settlement funds** on behalf of Coloradans struggling with opioid addiction. And _the way we’ve managed those funds_ is far more than just a win on paper; it’s meant a better life for many Coloradans — and saving lives. **We made sure 90% of the settlement funds were spent at the local and regional level, so communities could get their needs met** — without bottlenecks or barriers to addiction recovery, prevention, and treatment. That strategy worked — and I joined Sheriff Jackson in the summer of 2024 at the opening of the first drug treatment center in the San Luis Valley in a very long time. **And, in 2024, Colorado saw a 30% reduction in fentanyl overdose deaths — that's 350 lives saved from avoided fentanyl overdose deaths alone.** There’s so much more to do — and as our next governor, continuing to tackle our addiction crisis will be a top priority for me. Whether it’s building trust in government by publicly demonstrating how every settlement dollar is spent, or taking the Trump administration to court and winning when they try to illegally withhold federal dollars we need for investing in our public health, I’m taking action. As our next governor, I’ll keep delivering. **[We’ve seen too many Coloradans suffer because the Sackler family, Purdue Pharma, and many others used lies and deceit to turn a massive profit. If you believe our state deserves a governor who will defend our families, friends, and neighbors against abuse from irresponsible corporations and work to deliver results for all of us, I’d be honored to earn your donation>>>](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/117918370/578067691/-1377276739?refcode=em_WEI_FR_OpioidCrisis_102425&&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjYjFiZmM4Ni1mMmIwLWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=XVfWXVEesWs31sLa_new8m093cuBsjuttEI2i1Qz0Oo=)** Let’s get to work, Phil

name: Patrick J. Murphy
subject: From the Front with Patrick J. Murphy: Building Resilient Communities and Speaking Hard Truths
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP25/1/106220/images/PJM_Logo.png]
Hi Friends,
It’s been a meaningful week of reflection, connection, and purpose.
I turned 52 on Sunday, and I’m feeling deeply grateful for the people and work that make each year richer.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP25/1/106220/images/jack%20and%20pjm%2010.23.jpg]
In the Media: Calling for Responsibility in Washington
Yesterday afternoon at 3 PM on The Story with Martha MacCallum , I joined Fox News to talk about the need for leaders to dial back the rhetoric less than two months after Charlie Kirk’s assassination.
My message was clear: our democracy only works when we treat one another as fellow Americans, not enemies.
Leadership means lowering the temperature, not lighting more fires.
Political violence is unacceptable in any part of America, especially in the upper echelons of our government.
On Substack: Is Washington Even Listening?
In this week’s Substack column [https://patrickmurphypa.substack.com/p/is-washington-even-listening] , I wrote about the ongoing government shutdown and asked a simple question: Is anyone in Washington truly listening to the people they serve? We need to cultivate more leaders who believe public service is sacred.
Read the full essay → Is Washington Even Listening? [https://patrickmurphypa.substack.com/p/is-washington-even-listening]
Building Resilient Communities
Yesterday I was in Las Vegas where, I spoke at MCON on “Building Resilient Communities: VSO & Brand Collaboration for Military Families” and then did a fireside chat with the first woman Commander in Chief of the VFW, fellow Iraq Veteran Carol Whitmore on “Leading from the Front: Breaking Barriers & Building Bridges.”
I joined leaders from across the country to discuss how veterans’ organizations, our government and the private sector can strengthen the foundation of military families, communities and the challenges we face today in America.
Real change happens when mission-driven people work together.
Tune in → MCON Schedule [https://mcon.live/schedule/session-c-building-resilient-communities-vso-brand-collaboration-for-military-families]
On the Road: NYC Meetings and Podcasts
Earlier this week, we taped our weekly ‘Warrior Money’ show for Yahoo Finance and another one for Hilco Global on sovereign debt with my Wharton colleague Dr. Jessica Wachter.
From policy discussions to leadership conversations, my main focus always remains on bridging public service and private innovation to strengthen America to meet today’s challenges.
Stay tuned for more details when these episodes go live.
Our work continues to focus on building trust, showing courage, and reminding us that service is not a season of life, it’s a way of life.
Thank you for being part of our team.
Honorable Patrick J. Murphy

name: David Pan
subject: Please Vote No on Prop 50!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by David Pan for Congress 2026 [5]
body:
Please Vote No on Prop 50!

This is David Pan. I ran for Congress in the 46th district in 2024,
and I am running again in 2026.

I am writing today because you should have received your ballot for
this year’s election. There is only one question on that ballot:
whether to vote Yes or No on Proposition 50. I want to urge you to
vote NO on Prop 50.

This Proposition would change the boundaries of California’s
congressional districts to reduce the number of Republican
representatives from 9 down to 4 out of 52. It eliminates the district
that were drafted by an independent commission based on the boundaries
of local communities. Instead, we would have districts drawn by
Democratic Party consultants with the sole purpose of increasing the
number of seats in which Democrats will have a solid majority. This
“gerrymandering” of the district boundaries reduces the number of
competitive seats and undermines our election process. If you want to
vote in an election where your vote counts, you should vote No on Prop
50.

For over 10 years, California has had policies that have increased our
problems of homelessness, crime, and affordability.

· Homelessness has INCREASED BY 65% SINCE 2014
(https://eot.davidpanforcongress.org/f/a/uLfSVRH8ZIWmK3VhXKB7Tg~~/AAAHURA~/rbn8_bgNn1r87RJKqv2bROjPNXiHA_1r-NCRphTH7zCOIQt5E9gEIq52pe3eon5p_fwoJsRlOG8dVjyh9xNrxdK36JwtZ6WILKh0HKfIav045OKDhL2UNLxUcEl5J_t7yeNRA_i8mVZpHMc1mZxcCJKdx8VMnoVkOcogKiALDD5KwAonyC5fU4EyzB7jYu9eBNR_BN_i5nY9weHBgSqyQg~~
[1]), even though the state spends $5 TO $7 BILLION PER YEAR
(https://eot.davidpanforcongress.org/f/a/buhedqcRsB0Kom-Lyfjw0w~~/AAAHURA~/yzskO1bzuyVPEkRM4Rk85btj-aAaSzHfLvN07qSlDuEV6D8in_BMU5DUbAKT4kJlF0jLgdWC6cdNKh2V3IFJpzTboY0MrhGyGcMxsTf_fwN4p7wHMWxW_r7SGZT5zwNkp5uJCJQMMqh5pPOegn_uGtnUtOnvvpEKFfYS-vWa2-nmEi_gUKsTB0Tx3gHXVzDqWYpePBefdw-q2DD_cjabXqMKLXqfv84TjHwkxfMOQSE~
[2]) on the problem.

· The violent crime rate increased in that period. It
was already 15% higher than in the rest of the nation. Now our violent
crime rate is 31% HIGHER THAN NATIONWIDE
(https://eot.davidpanforcongress.org/f/a/m4UFLumaQ2bJcsn0y14IXw~~/AAAHURA~/Gb9So2OVujLv9m7J3ERXUg3vdkBjVjQGR1nxrbkgxdvJnEzqyUJTmoH__Ypoh2en4jHFZOtZbEhF2PWFRukne951E0cmbQ6lsuKAed9urK_YnGv8RgC6tIfLnVfHkDZk5nyP2yaihIodSwAcQtD8n8U8jYGhMmsCApO0bu7lWF2XZz28j7IkswN1c_iv4c-w6iIc0aFc0GhcAndOZ22IDw~~
[3]).

· We have all seen gas prices go up relentlessly to
$5 and $6 per gallon, with more increases on the way if our policies
do not change.

· The dream of owning a home has slipped away from
most Californians, especially our young people, due to policies that
prevent and delay construction of new towns and cities.

If we want to have serious discussions of alternatives, we need to
maintain competitive districts in which candidates have to earn your
vote. Vote No on Prop 50.

Please also consider making a donation to my campaign for Congress in
the 46th district, covering Santa Ana, Anaheim, Stanton, and parts of
Fullerton and Orange. Your $5 will make a difference. Please go to
davidpanforcongress.com [4]

| | **Last week, Transportation and Infrastructure Democrats met with the National Air Traffic Controller Association president to learn more about the shutdown's impact on air traffic controllers.** **[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/117921141/578077748/1596212816?refcode=2025-10-24-shutdown&recurring=&amount=19&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=0bddaddd-f5b0-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYmRkYWRkZC1mNWIwLWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=zPlwIXL2_gBBCnMGLiRSC3hJvvfWuT7DpqrNEZlRC4s=)** Air traffic controllers are committed to your safety, and as of today, and every day this government shutdown continues, they are not getting paid. And yet, they are still showing up for work. Rather than working to reopen the government to ensure air traffic controllers get paid, the Republican White House is scrutinizing workers who are calling in sick and threatening to fire them. These threats will only make things worse. **We can not afford to lose more workers from an already depleted air traffic controller workforce.** Instead of blaming the people we rely on to safely transport the flying public, the Trump administration should come to the negotiating table. # [We don't quit: Michigan manufacturing and the fight ahead](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=177024855&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTc3MDI0ODU1LCJpYXQiOjE3NjEzMjMyMzcsImV4cCI6MTc2MzkxNTIzNywiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.PPUR9WBQgZaQePxWHXFytFg5ndKW62-HnJEvF_ELhsU)
### This is grit.
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Oct 24
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack..OqISdz_A1iF-_9XITmjTFIEyIM8_v8LkjBrQUGfSGAc?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/we-dont-quit-michigan-manufacturing?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Let me tell you something I know for certain: **Manufacturing made Michigan - **_**and Michigan made me.**_
I was born and raised in Michigan, and I've been surrounded by this industry my whole life. From the shop floors to the shipping docks, from Auburn Hills to Grand Rapids, we're not just talking about a 9 to 5 job - we're talking about a way of life. About a career you can raise a family on. About pride in building something with your own two hands. About what it means to be from Michigan.
It's not always been easy. There have always been people, pundits, and politicians who have doubted Michigan manufacturing. That's not me - and that's not the hardworking people of Michigan. We don't walk away from challenges. **We rise to meet them.**
To the doubters, I say: Come see Michigan. Come walk the floor of an auto plant. Talk to the folks who never gave up on Michigan manufacturing, who've trained the next generation with calloused hands and open hearts. **This is the Michigan way: Grease, grit, and hard work.**_**It 's who we are.**_
And yes, we're in a tough moment. The Trump administration's tariffs are putting strain on our auto industry. Supply chains are still recovering. And overseas competition is taking aim at American-made goods. That's why our manufacturing sector deserves an advocate in the U.S. Senate.
I've spent my career fighting for this state and this industry. I helped lead the auto rescue under President Obama in 2008 - when people were writing Detroit off, we rolled up our sleeves and helped save over 200,000 jobs.
In Congress, I've worked to bring manufacturing jobs back to Michigan and strengthen workforce training programs. Always side by side with union workers. Always pushing for legislation that will help Michiganders thrive.
We are a state whose economy is still driven centrally by manufacturing. That's not a flaw - it's a strength. There's pride in the work, pride in the skilled workforce, and pride in knowing that we're building the future, brick by brick.
When I travel across Michigan, from Detroit to Flint, from Lansing to Traverse City, I see that pride. There's a sense of unity. We came back. **That 's Michigan grit**.
That's why I'm running for Senate. To be a champion for Michigan manufacturing. To fight like hell for our working families. And to make sure our kids grow up in a state that builds the future.
So if you believe, like I do, that Michigan manufacturing is worth fighting for, I hope you'll consider making a contribution to support this campaign.
[Donate](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/c3fafdc4-59db-428e-9331-c47c33d89581?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We've got a long road ahead - but we're Michigan. Grit is what we do. We build. We fight. We never give up.
Let's do it together.
Haley

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
[Donate](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/aa4d623f-a9f6-47c9-be76-d79fde1dca5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Peter, We don’t need to tell you that Donald Trump is out of touch. It grows more apparent by the day that the only people he’s prioritizing are himself and his wealthy friends. People are struggling to afford groceries, but Trump would rather host a lavish fundraiser at Mar-a-Lago than make life easier for working people. Americans are losing their healthcare, but Trump is moving forward with the construction of his $250 million ballroom in the White House. # Did you know?

Voters in Georgia could face legal issues if they are unaware of the state's residency laws. If you move within Georgia, it's essential to update your voter registration with your new address. This ensures you receive the correct ballot for your district. You can update your registration online, by mail, or in person. Just remember to do this at least **29 days before an election** to ensure you can vote in your new precinct!
---
|
---
---
| |
# The Most Consequential Race of 2026
As I’ve said before, the Secretary of State race is the most consequential race of 2026 — and we’re taking this campaign very seriously.

Since filing to run in July, our team has been laser-focused. In just three months, we’ve visited more than a dozen counties across Georgia and joined several prominent shows — including The Martha Zoller Show, The Morning Xtra, Austin Rhodes, and Shelley Wynter — to discuss why this race matters and how I plan to restore leadership, accountability, and integrity to this office.

On Tuesday, October 7th, we officially launched our campaign at Park Bench in Marietta, GA (The Battery) with over 200 friends, family, and supporters in attendance — and reached more than 25,000 voters who tuned in live to watch my speech.

This campaign is about restoring trust in Georgia’s election process and ensuring every voice is heard. Our momentum is growing, and we’re just getting started!
---
|

---
| Following our kickoff, we hosted industry roundtables with business leaders across the state to identify ways to cut red tape and strengthen Georgia’s position as the best state to do business in. These discussions have been invaluable — and we have more to come! Click the **Join the Table** button below to sign up and receive notifications about upcoming roundtable events.

Last week, I met with voters and local leaders in Big Canoe (Pickens & Dawson Counties), Paulding, Forsyth, and Cherokee. I’m committed to showing up, listening, and doing the work — just as I did when serving our country in the Air Force.

You’re supporting a campaign that values service, transparency, and hard work. Together, we can ensure that every vote counts, every business is protected, and every investment in Georgia’s future is secure.

Help us keep the momentum going-- spread the word, donate if you’re able, and volunteer if you feel called

I know my team and I have reached out about deadlines like this before, but we could really use your help.

**June 5, 2018.**
Do you remember it? I'll never forget it — that was the day we launched our first campaign for Congress.
The truth is, I had no idea what to expect.
I knew we had a large number of supporters who would be willing to commit the time and hard work needed to run a campaign of that magnitude, but I also knew that one of the biggest challenges we'd face would be funding a winning campaign.
But because of supporters like you, that was never in doubt. We were able to organize and mobilize our movement in Minnesota's 5th district, fighting off unprecedented right-wing attacks and outside spending along the way.
Two years later in 2020 we did it again. And again in 2022 and 2024.
**Midnight, October 31st.**
A week from now — our next fundraising deadline.
I know my team and I have reached out about deadlines like this before, but it’s really important that we have a big show of momentum as Super PACs and anti-progressive billionaires decide if they will back a candidate in this race.
But the truth is, we’re still behind our goal. At least $15,000 behind.
**$5.**
That's the amount I'm asking you to contribute right now to stand with our movement, close our fundraising gap, and get the job done.
Are you in?
